clue.text: Never to be beaten at home with half home and board

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'she is in'

indicators.note: half signals that only the first four of the eight letters of the synonym are kept

parts.note: a home is a domicile
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A team that is never beaten on its own ground, given food and lodging there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first four letters of an eight-letter word for home; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconquerable can never be beaten or subdued.

clue.text: See 7
Rich man takes plunge

definitions.meaning: the traditional name for the rich man in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus
jumps headfirst into water, as a swimmer does

explanation.definitionFit: Dives is the Latin word for rich, used as a name for the parable's rich man; a diver plunges.

clue.text: See 7
Landseer's monarchy's end could be lengthened

indicators.note: could be says the letters of one word, with another's removed, can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters to rearrange
taken as written, the letters taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A painter's kingdom might be stretched out at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Landseer painted The Monarch of the Glen, a famous Victorian picture of a stag; the stag's domain is its monarchy. The answer plus END rearranges to LENGTHENED.
explanation.definitionFit: The stag in Landseer's painting reigns over a Scottish valley, so that valley is its kingdom.

clue.text: Travel light to support Wolves?

parts.note: to support someone is to back them
wolves hunt in a pack

explanation.surface: Is going with little luggage a way of cheering on the Wolves football team?
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, a British team; here it is just a group of wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpack is to travel cheaply carrying everything in a rucksack.

clue.text: Laboratory worker to be entertaining fairy not right in the head

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to be is to exist
a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
mentally unbalanced, colloquially mental

explanation.surface: A lab scientist hosts a mad fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who carries out tests and trials in a laboratory is one who experiments.

clue.text: Deference pays, big time (not so much among flowers: a strong scent keeps subject out): you must back call for silence (exhausted female taking it hard) after you are old (incorrectly)

indicators.note: after sends the letter for hard behind the archaic phrase, to the very end
among says one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: a flower bed holds flowers, so flowers gives bed
not so much means less
taken as written

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the scent encloses the subject

parts.note: a strong unpleasant smell is a reek
a subject is a theme
to back something is to be for it
they is used for people in general, as is you in 'you never know'
sh is the call for quiet
exhausted means all in
her is a female pronoun
taken as written
thou art is the archaic form of you are; using thee there is the incorrect version
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A long rambling instruction about respect, flowers, smells and silencing a tired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition paraphrases the Beatitude 'Blessed are the meek': humility is hugely rewarded. Flowers grow in a bed; 'must', 'taking' and 'out' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitude promises that the humble shall receive the whole world, so humility pays off hugely.

clue.text: Cry of relief from Frank Capra! Is Ethel or Doris Waters involved?

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside the following words

parts.words: Capra! Is Ethel or Doris Waters

explanation.surface: A film director and two music-hall comediennes take part in a joyful exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Capra was a Hollywood director; Doris Waters was half of a British comedy double act. The answer runs from caPRA through to the D of Doris.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclaiming gratitude to God is what people cry out when something bad has been avoided.

clue.text: What did you say in the loo about port?

indicators.note: in places the query inside the toilet

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, the loo
eh is the query when you have not heard
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone shouts from the toilet, mishearing a question about a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo and lav are informal British words for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A major French port on the Channel at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: I get away with directions to skip

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
S is the compass abbreviation for south
to skip about is to caper

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can run off with instructions to jump around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: 'I' is the one who gets away.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gets away from captivity is a runaway or fugitive.

clue.text: It's far from calming to emphasise the possibility of flu

parts.note: to emphasise is to stress

indicators.note: the possibility of signals the letters could form another arrangement

explanation.surface: Worrying about catching flu is anything but soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the possibility of' rearranges FLU into FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that causes anxiety and tension is the opposite of calming.

clue.text: Religious man's reluctance to spend if he has a lot of money

indicators.note: the religious man, if he has the extra letters, makes the longer word; so they are taken away

parts.note: parsimony is meanness with money

indicators.note: a lot of means most of, so the word loses one letter

explanation.surface: A believer's stinginess seems odd for a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of money' is MONEY without its E, MONY; PARSI plus MONY makes PARSIMONY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism in India, descended from Persians.

clue.text: Food, eggs and toasted sandwiches (starters)

indicators.note: starters means the opening letters of the listed words

explanation.surface: A menu of eggs and toasted sandwiches as starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is a colloquial word for food.

clue.text: Beer's neighbour refuses company award

parts.note: bran is husk waste, refuse; plural brans
an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A drinker's neighbour turns down a firm's prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Beer is a village on the Devon coast in England; Branscombe is the next village along, so 'Beer' is not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Branscombe lies beside Beer on the east Devon coast, making it its neighbour.

clue.text: Could be cloudier but still needs to be refined

indicators.note: could be says the letters may form another word

explanation.surface: Something might be murkier yet still require polishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum straight from the ground must be processed in a refinery before use.

clue.text: Carbon here may be a loathsome thing

indicators.note: may be says these letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Carbon here may be something hateful, like a pollutant.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrence can mean an object of loathing as well as the loathing itself.

clue.text: Ask headless chicken to party

indicators.note: headless means losing the first letter

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
a treat is an outing or party

explanation.surface: Asking a chicken that has lost its head to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly, to beg or plead.

clue.text: Native American dish on a seat near the ground

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: Native American food served on a low stool.
explanation.walkthrough: A creepie is a low stool, a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A creepie is a low three-legged stool, a seat set close to the floor.

clue.text: Little distance from island

definitions.meaning: a short distance, about two and a half centimetres
a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny measure of length; in Scotland, an inch is also a small island.

clue.text: To alter a text is something tremendous

indicators.note: something here means part of the following word, a piece inside it

explanation.surface: Editing a document is a tremendous task.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or revise a written text.

clue.text: See 7
Second left and I'm on my way to the county

parts.note: I'm gives the letter I
to be on your way is to go

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for the county, second-left turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Reciting "The Harlot's Lament" may be a stimulus

indicators.note: reciting means saying out loud, so the sound matters

parts.note: a harlot is a whore and a lament is a moan

explanation.surface: Performing a poem titled for a prostitute's sorrow might arouse an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A hormone is a chemical messenger that stimulates activity in the body.

clue.text: Sidney's battle in France unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is lost

parts.note: Poitiers, 1356, an English victory in the Hundred Years War

explanation.surface: A man's war story from France is not complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney Poitier was the Hollywood actor; the possessive definition matches 'Sidney's' surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney's surname: the Bahamian-American actor Sidney Poitier.

clue.text: Be a locum at hospital — past crime, seizing gold

parts.note: past means old, former

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: theft is a crime
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor at hospital has an old robbery involving gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold the fort is to look after things while someone is away, as a locum does.
